audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL execution mechanics (LOG opcodes, gas refunds, RIPEMD-160 precompile, block validation, transaction types, Merkle proofs, chain ID), CL integration (beacon chain withdrawals, fork activation, BLS remote signing), and wallet/application layer interfaces (silent signing, RPC).

misclassified_entities.reason: Governance entity, not a runtime data source interacting with EL/CL at system boundaries. Relevant to hard fork process (EIP-233) but does not send data into the system under audit.
Governance entity, not a runtime external entity. EIP authors propose specifications but do not interact with the system at runtime.
Development teams, not runtime data sources. They implement software but do not send data into the running system.
System contracts execute within the EL as part of block processing. They are internal components, not external entities.
Internal component of the BLS signer request handling pipeline, not an external entity.
In EIP-5345 context, the user interacts with the wallet UI locally. The wallet is the system boundary; user consent is an internal wallet process, not an external data flow into EL/CL.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client via eth_getProof
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any external client can invoke eth_getProof over unauthenticated JSON-RPC. Request parameters (address, storage keys, block ID) must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client via eth_chainId
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated public RPC call. While read-only, the response is security-critical for replay protection (EIP-155).

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Provider (Untrusted Proof Source)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: RPC providers returning Merkle proofs are untrusted. Proof data must be cryptographically verified against a trusted stateRoot before use.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (block headers, withdrawals, beacon block root)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated via JWT. The CL provides block data including withdrawals and parent_beacon_block_root. Content must still be validated (withdrawal indices, amounts, roots).

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer / Validator via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Blocks received from P2P peers are fully untrusted. All header fields, transaction roots, withdrawals roots, and requests hashes must be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Network Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes may be malicious. All block and transaction data propagated over P2P is untrusted and requires full validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract/EOA Calling Precompile
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract or EOA can invoke precompiles with arbitrary input data. Gas metering must prevent DoS; input is arbitrary bytes.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Application via eth_chainId
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth_chainId JSON-RPC for transaction signing context
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Wallet queries chain ID for replay protection. The wallet is external; if connected to a compromised node, it receives incorrect chain ID.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via wallet_requestSilentSign / wallet_silentSignTransaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps requesting silent signing permissions are untrusted. Permission scope, secret validation, and temporal bounds must be enforced by the wallet.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator Client via BLS Remote Signer API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validator clients should be authenticated (TLS + ACLs), but the signer must still validate request format, BLS domain, and ideally enforce slashing protection. Authentication channel exists but content validation is required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Layer for BLS Signer
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: HTTP interface to BLS remote signer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network traffic to the BLS signer may be intercepted or injected if not using TLS. Unauthenticated requests from the network are fully untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: HSM / Secrets Manager
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Key retrieval interface (HSM API or secrets manager API)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The HSM is authenticated and expected to securely store keys, but the signer must handle key loading errors and ensure keys are zeroized after use. Trust is conditional on correct HSM configuration.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer / Light Client (Trusted Header Source)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block header provision for proof verification
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Light clients or beacon chain provide trusted block headers with stateRoot. The source is authenticated via consensus protocol, but header freshness and correctness depend on sync state.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All request parameters (address, storage keys, block identifier) must be validated. Resource limits must prevent DoS via excessive storage key requests.
Request format validation required. Response must accurately reflect current chain configuration.
All proof data must be cryptographically verified against a trusted stateRoot. No proof data should be trusted without hash verification.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API (newPayload, forkchoiceUpdated) providing withdrawals and beacon block root
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Withdrawal indices must be sequential, amounts must be valid. Withdrawals root must match header commitment. Parent beacon block root must be validated.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block header decode and validation pipeline
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full header validation required: parent_hash, state_root, transactions_root, receipt_root, withdrawals_root, requests_hash, blob gas fields. Any invalid field must cause block rejection.
All blocks and transactions from peers require full validation. Eclipse attack mitigations must be in place.
Gas must be correctly charged (base + per-word cost) before execution. Arbitrary input length must be handled safely. Output must be deterministic.
Wallet must verify chain ID matches expected network before signing. Node must return correct chain ID for current head block.

Permission scope (chain ID, contract address, function signatures, timestamp) must be validated. User consent must be obtained. Permission secret must be cryptographically random with sufficient entropy.
Permission secret must be verified. Transaction must be within granted scope (contract, function, chain). Temporal bounds must be enforced.
Request authentication required. BLS domain must be validated (beacon_proposer, beacon_attester, randao). Key identifier must exist. Slashing protection must be enforced externally.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: HTTP interface to BLS remote signer
boundary_edges.security_assumption: TLS must be used for transport encryption. Authentication and rate limiting must be enforced. No signing requests should be processed from unauthenticated sources.
Key material must be encrypted at rest. Keys loaded into memory must be zeroized after use. HSM must be properly configured with access controls.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block header provision (stateRoot for proof verification)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Header must be obtained from a trusted consensus source. Stale or forged headers would allow fraudulent proof verification.
